L0@P0: ATCC Medium: 2467 MS-OCM Base Medium
L1@P0: Sodium bicarbonate…………………………………8.4 g
L2@P0: DI Water………………………………………………976.0 ml
L3@P0: Dissolve sodium bicarbonate in deionized water (100 mM Na2HCO3). Bubble
L4@P0: solution with an oxygen-free gas mixture of N2-CO2 (70:30). While gassing, add
L5@P0: 10 ml of Solutions A (see below) and 2 ml of Solution B (see below). The high
L6@P0: initial pH of this solution may cause the minerals to precipitate. As the pH
L7@P0: decreases as a result of equilibration of the CO2: bicarbonate buffering system,
L8@P0: the minerals will go back into solution; at the same time O2 is driven out of the
L9@P0: medium. Next, add and dissolve dry ingredients in the order listed:
L10@P0: Yeast extract…………………………………………..2.0 g
L11@P0: Trypticase peptones………………………………….2.0 g
L12@P0: The medium is allowed to gas until it has become clear, usually 30 to 60 minutes
L13@P0: depending on the gas flow rate. The pH of the clear medium should be between
L14@P0: pH 7 and pH 7.3. At this point add 2 ml of Solution C (see below) and 10 ml of
L15@P0: Trace Minerals Supplement (available from ATCC, cat. MD-TMS) to the medium.
L16@P0: The medium is then ready to be transferred to culture tubes. Dispense with
L17@P0: continual gassing. After the all tubes are filled, capped, and crimped, autoclave
L18@P0: the medium at 121ºC. Following autoclaving a precipitate may form; with periodic
L19@P0: mixing this should go back into solution within 48 hours.
L20@P0: Solution A
L21@P0: (100X solution; use 10 ml of solution A per liter of medium)
L22@P0: Ammonium chloride……………………………………..100.0 g
L23@P0: Magnesium chloride hexahydrate……………………..100.0 g
L24@P0: Calcium chloride dehydrate…………………………….40.0 g
L25@P0: DI Water…………………………………………………..up to 1000.0 ml
L26@P0: Dissolve in deionized water, adjust pH to 4.0 with HCl and bring up to one liter.
L27@P0: Solution B
L28@P0: (500X solution; use 2 ml of solution B per liter of medium)
L29@P0: Potassium dibasic phosphate trihydrate……………….200.0 g
L30@P0: DI Water……………………………………………………up to 1000.0 ml
L31@P0: Dissolve in deionized water then bring the volume up to one liter.
L32@P0: Solution C
L33@P0: (500X; use 2 ml of solution C per liter of medium)
L34@P0: Resazurin…………………………………………………0.5 g
L35@P0-1: DI Water……………………………………………………up to 1000.0 mlDissolve in deionized water, and then bring the volume up to one liter.
L36@P1: Reducing Agents
L37@P1: We suggest adding the reducing agent to the medium at least one hour before the
L38@P1: medium is to be inoculated.
L39@P1: Co-enzyme M (mercaptoethanesulfonic acid) Solution (100 X solution)
L40@P1: Mercaptoethanesulfonic acid…………………….5.0 g
L41@P1: DI Water…………………………………………….100 ml
L42@P1: Distribute into screw cap test tubes, 5–6 ml per tube and seal with rubber
L43@P1: stoppers under N2 gas. Autoclave at 121ºC to sterilize. Excess tubes can be
L44@P1: stored at room temperature for up to 2 months. Co-enzyme M is a compound
L45@P1: produced by many methanogens. Some methanogens are sensitive to stronger
L46@P1: reducing agents such as sodium sulfide. Co-enzyme M is the standard reducing
L47@P1: agent we use when working with methanogens.
L48@P1: Sodium Sulfide Solution (100 X solution)
L49@P1: Sodium sulfide nonahydrate……………………..1.5 g
L50@P1: DI Water…………………………………………….100 ml
L51@P1: Distribute into screw cap test tubes, 5–6 ml per tube, and seal with Hungate
L52@P1: stoppers. Autoclave at 121ºC to sterilize. Excess tubes can be stored frozen for
L53@P1: up to 6 months. Once thawed a tube of sodium sulfide should not be used for
L54@P1: more than a week. CAUTON: if sodium sulfide comes into contact with a strong
L55@P1: acid, hydrogen sulfide (H2S), a very toxic gas is liberated immediately.
L56@P1: Cysteine Solution (100X solution)
L57@P1: Cysteine……………………………………………..3.0 g
L58@P1: DI Water……………………………………………...100 ml
L59@P1: Distribute into screw cap test tubes, 5–6 ml per tube, and seal with Hungate
L60@P1: stoppers. Autoclave at 121ºC to sterilize. Excess tubes can be stored frozen for
L61@P1: up to 6 months. Once thawed, a tube of cysteine should not be used for more
L62@P1: than a week.

L0@P0: ATCC Medium: 2485 MH-OCM Medium
L1@P0: MS-OCM Base Medium Solution A: (100X solution; use 10 ml of solution A per liter of medium)  Ammonium chloride………………………………………. 100.0 g  Magnesium chloride hexahydrate…………………………. 100.0 g  Calcium chloride dehydrate………………………………... 40.00 g  Distilled Water …………………………………………… ….1.0 L Dissolve in deionized water, adjust pH to 4.0 with HCl and bring up to one liter.
L2@P0: Solution B: (500X solution; use 2 ml of solution B per liter of medium)  Potassium dibasic phosphate trihydrate …………………………200.0 g  Distilled Water …………………………………………………….1.0L  Dissolve in deionized water then bring the volume up to one liter. Solution C: (500X; use 2 ml of solution C per liter of medium)  Resazurin………………………………………………… 0.5 g  Distilled Water ……………………………………………1.0L Dissolve in deionized water, then bring the volume up to one liter. Trace Mineral Supplement, Catalog No.
L3@P0: MD-TMS: (Available from ATCC as a sterile ready-to-use liquid.) per liter of medium……………………………………10.0 ml To prepare the medium dissolve 8.4 gm sodium bicarbonate in 976.0 ml of deionized water (100 mM Na2HCO3). The solution is bubbled with an oxygen-free gas
L4@P0: mixture of N2-CO2 (70:30). While gassing, the stock solutions A and B are added. The high initial pH of this solution may cause the minerals to precipitate. As
L5@P0: the pH decreases as a result of equilibration of the CO2:bicarbonate buffering system the minerals will go back into solution; at the same time O2 is driven out of
L6@P0-1: the medium. Dry ingredients are also added and dissolved in the order listed. Add:
L7@P1:  Sodium bicarbonate………………………………8.4g  Yeast extract …………………………………….2.0 g  Trypticase peptone…………………………… ...2.0 g
L8@P1: NaCl…………………………………… ….....87.75 g MgCl2 x 7H2O…………………………………....5.0g
L9@P1:  KCl…………………………………………. …...1.5g  Distilled Water……………………………… 976.0mL The medium is allowed to gas until it has become clear, usually 30 to 60 minutes depending on the gas flow rate. The pH of the cleared medium should be
L10@P1: between pH 7 and pH 7.3. At this point the solution C and trace minerals supplement can be added to the medium. The medium is then ready to be transferred to culture tubes. For this purpose, a gas-cannula system with at least three separate gassing ports should be used. A rack of Balch tubes should be made ready. The flask of medium is continuously gassed with one gas cannula; the other two cannula are placed, one each, in two sequential Balch tubes.
L11@P1: A 10 ml pipette is used to pipette 10 ml of medium from the flask to the 1st Balch tube. The cannula is then removed from this tube and at
L12@P1: the same time a butyl rubber stopper is pushed into the top; it is important to do this all in one motion to minimize contamination of the headspace of the tube with air. This cannula is then moved to the 3rd tube in sequence and the 2nd tube is filled with media and capped, and so on. After the all tubes are filled, capped, and
L13@P1: crimped, the medium can be autoclaved. Following autoclaving a precipitate may form; with periodic mixing this should go back into solution within 48 hours.Note: In our experience, the resazurin is often colorless after autoclaving MS medium, probably because the yeast extract provides enough reducing power to cause complete reduction of the dye. We still recommend adding a reducing agent to the medium. Reducing agents:
L14@P1:  We suggest adding the reducing agent to the medium at least one hour before the medium is to be inoculated. Co-enzyme M (mercaptoethanesulfonic acid) (100 X solution): Dissolve 5.0 g in 100 ml of deionized water. Distribute into screw cap test tubes, 5–6 ml per tube
L15@P1: and seal with rubber stoppers under N2 gas. Autoclave to sterilize. Excess tubes can be stored at room temperature for up to 2 months. Co-enzyme M is a
L16@P1: compound produced by many methanogens. Some methanogens are sensitive to stronger reducing agents such as sodium sulfide. Co-enzyme M is the standard reducing agent we use when working with methanogens. Sodium sulfide (100 X solution): Dissolve 1.5 g in 100 ml of distilled water. Distribute into screw cap test tubes, 5–6 ml per tube, and seal with Hungate stoppers. Autoclave to sterilize. Excess tubes can be stored frozen for up to 6 months.
L17@P1-2: Once thawed a tube of sodium sulfide should not be used for more than a week. CAUTON: if sodium sulfide comes into contact with a strong acid, hydrogen sulfide (H2S), a very toxic gas is liberated immediately.Cysteine (100X solution): Dissolve 3.0 g in 100 ml of distilled water. Distribute into screw cap test tubes, 5–6 ml per tube, and seal with Hungate stoppers.
L18@P2: Autoclave to sterilize. Excess tubes can be stored frozen for up to 6 months. Once thawed, a tube of cysteine should not be used for more than a week.
